messages.subject: Translating structural equation model from JAGS to Stan
parts:
Hi all,

I'm currently trying to transition from JAGS to Stan and am therefore re-specifying some basic models I need in my analysis. When I'm running my model (with RStan), I get error messages that seem to indicate something's wrong with my initial values:

[1] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                        
  [2] "Exception thrown at line 25: normal_log: Location parameter is nan, but must be finite!"                                               
  [3] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
  [4] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                              
  [5] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                              
  [6] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."

However, I do not know how to proceed from here or how to specify appropriate initial values. I would appreciate any hints of what might be wrong with my model.

data {
  int<lower=1> N; // number of participants
  int<lower=1> K; // number of variables
  int<lower=1> L; // number of latent variables
  matrix[N,K] Y; // data
}

parameters{
  vector<lower=1>[K] theta; // error residual variances
  vector<lower=1>[L] psi; //latent variable variances
  matrix[N,L+1] eta; // LVs
}

model{

  vector[K+L-1] lambda; //  factor loadings
  vector[K] nu; // manifest variable intercepts
  vector[L] alpha; // latent variable intercepts
  matrix[N,K] mu; // MVs
  matrix [N,L+1] mu_eta; // mean of LVs
 
  for (i in 1:N){
    for (j in 1:K){
      Y[i,j] ~ normal(mu[i,j],theta[j]);
    }
 
    mu[i,1] = nu[1]+lambda[1]*eta[i,2];
    mu[i,2] = nu[2]+lambda[2]*eta[i,2];
    mu[i,3] = nu[3]+lambda[3]*eta[i,2];
    mu[i,4] = nu[4]+lambda[4]*eta[i,2];
    mu[i,5] = nu[5]+lambda[5]*eta[i,3];
    mu[i,6] = nu[6]+lambda[6]*eta[i,3];
   
    // Can I vectorize this part?
    eta[i,1] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,1],psi[1]);
    eta[i,2] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,2],psi[2]);
    eta[i,3] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,3],psi[3]);
    eta[i,4] ~ normal(mu_eta[i,4],psi[4]);
    mu_eta[i,1] = alpha[1];
    mu_eta[i,2] = alpha[2] + lambda[19]*eta[i,1];
    mu_eta[i,3] = alpha[3] + lambda[20]*eta[i,1];
    mu_eta[i,4] = alpha[4] + lambda[21]*eta[i,1];
   
    // Intercepts
    nu[K] = 0;
    alpha[L] = 0;
   
    // Loadings
    lambda[1] = 1;
    lambda[2] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[3] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[4] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[5] = 1;
    lambda[6] = 1;
    lambda[7] = 1;
    lambda[8] = 1;
   
    // Precision
    theta ~ gamma(1,.5);
    psi ~ gamma(1,.5);
  }
}

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Translating structural equation model from JAGS to Stan
parts:
Some of your lambdas seem to be data and some seem to be parameters.  I think you should split into two quantites:  data for the prespecified values and parameters for the unknowns.  In any case, yes you can define intermediate quantities in the model block, but, remember, the lines of Stan code are executed in order.  So if you want to define lambda[1] = 1, then you have to make that assignment _before_ you use lambda.  The assigment can be made in the model block but it should be before lambda is used.
A

On Saturday, October 15, 2016 at 10:20:56 PM UTC-4, Andrew Gelman wrote:
Some of your lambdas seem to be data and some seem to be parameters.  I think you should split into two quantites:  data for the prespecified values and parameters for the unknowns.  In any case, yes you can define intermediate quantities in the model block, but, remember, the lines of Stan code are executed in order.  So if you want to define lambda[1] = 1, then you have to make that assignment _before_ you use lambda.  The assigment can be made in the model block but it should be before lambda is used.

There is an example with fixed zeros rather than fixed ones at

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/7eiyZTjVMM4/qr8bXJ9daLoJ

But it would be easier to fix the latent variable variances (psi) to 1 and let the loadings be free.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Translating structural equation model from JAGS to Stan
parts:
Stan's a regular programming language, so variables must be
defined before they are used. You have this:

model{
...
vector[L] alpha; // latent variable intercepts

for (i in 1:N){

// Intercepts
nu[K] = 0;
alpha[L] = 0;

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

This redefines nu[K] and alpha[L], which are the last elements
of their respective vectors, in each loop

If you want to initialize these vectors to zero, do it outside the loop:

nu = rep_vector(0, K);
alpha = rep_vector(0, L);
for (n in 1:N) ...

- Bob

Whatever your eventual modeling goal, it helps from a software
perspective to start simple and build up one step at a time. It
sounds laborious, but it's more pleasant to try to extend a functioning
program than to locate a bug in a complex one. When you build from
working code, it helps to locate when and where you introduced a bug.

- Bob

    lambda[1] = 1;
    lambda[2] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[3] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[4] ~ normal(0,1);
    lambda[5] = 1;
    lambda[6] = 1;
    lambda[7] = 1;
    lambda[8] = 1;
   
    // Precision
    theta ~ gamma(1,.5);
    psi ~ gamma(1,.5);
  }
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Translating structural equation model from JAGS to Stan
parts:
Without knowing more specifics of the model, it's hard to
say much more than is in the manual, which is to
model missing data with a distribution and either code
the missing data as a parameter and impute its value
(only works for continuous params in Stan) or marginalize
out the missing data variables (more efficient and the only
option for discrete parameters in Stan).

If there's missing count data (e.g., Poisson-like) then
you probably won't be able to fit the missing data in Stan.

The alternative is to do multiple imputation externally then
fit multiple Stan models, but that's very compute intensive
and doesn't give you a coherent joint model of the data
and parameters.

- Bob
